Q: Which shell is it actually? A:

The default version of bash on macOS is very old (3.2 is from around ~2006), while zsh is kept up-to-date. This is probably due to Apple's issues with GPLv3.

While you can use an older version for basic programming, most online examples and tutorials are going to assume that you're using a current version. One workaround is to install a newer version of bash, or you can simply use zsh.

Personally I find zsh to be more programmer-friendly, but YMMV.

Q: CodeIgniter's order_by() incorrectly applies backticks to a CASE expression A:

I don't know about the first two major versions of CodeIgniter, but certainly the third offers an order_by() method which has 3 parameters.

public function order_by($orderby, $direction = '', $escape = NULL)

In your case, I don't think it is necessary to use a verbose CASE statement; just pass the IS NULL expression. The same effect will be rendered from the true/false evaluation.

$this->db->order_by('roll_number IS NULL', '', false);

...to follow up on your commented coding attempt...

Once you start getting into multiple tie breaker rules, a comma-separated string becomes difficult to read by a human eye. I might recommend that you express the rules using multiple lines and comments or an array with descriptive keys. I also think the rules can be refined a bit. SQLize Demo

$priorities = [
    'nulls last' => 'roll_number IS NULL',
    'whole numbers first otherwise hyphenateds lexicographically' => "CASE WHEN POSITION('-' IN roll_number) THEN roll_number END",
    'whole numbers naturally' => "CAST(TRIM(roll_number) AS SIGNED)",
];
$this->db->order_by(implode(',', $priorities), '', false) // whole numbers naturally

Or

$this->db
    ->order_by('roll_number IS NULL', '', false) // nulls last
    ->order_by("CASE WHEN POSITION('-' IN roll_number) THEN roll_number END", '', false) // whole numbers first otherwise hyphenateds lexicographically
    ->order_by('CAST(TRIM(roll_number) AS SIGNED)', '', false)

This provides an example result of:

| roll_number |
|-------------|
| 1           |
| 2           |
| 5           |
| 10          |
| 20          |
| 10-1        |
| 10-2        |
| 3-1         |
| 5-10        |
| [null]      |

I don't see how that is a useful sort, but I don't even know the sample data. I might have put:

  1. Nulls last,
  2. Leading integer naturally,
  3. Whole integers before hyphenateds,
  4. Trailing integer naturally

SQLize Demo

ORDER BY
    roll_number IS NULL,
    CAST(roll_number AS SIGNED),
    POSITION('-' IN roll_number) > 0,
    CAST(SUBSTRING(roll_number, '-', 1) AS SIGNED)

| roll_number |
|-------------|
| 1           |
| 2           |
| 3-1         |
| 5           |
| 5-10        |
| 10          |
| 10-1        |
| 10-2        |
| 20          |
| [null]      |
